Base monthly rent is the working total. Anything marked Unlisted is not published by the landlord or the listing service, and we confirm it directly before any comparison, because on your budget an unpriced expense is the difference between two spaces that look identical. Full-buildout spaces carry a medical or office fit-out benchmark of roughly $180 a foot, and a dental fit-out typically runs higher.

Palm Plaza, Suite 1039

Niceville, FL 32578
Address 1003-1047 East John Sims Parkway, Suite 1039, Niceville, FL 32578. Retail and office plaza in the heart of Niceville, daily traffic count near 40,000.

One of the two lowest base rents in the entire search, and the only space on this tour that lands squarely inside your target band without demising. The suite measures 25 feet by 100 feet with open retail across the front, one ADA restroom, and a storage area at the rear. Operating expenses are published at $2.02 a foot, which is the lowest here by a wide margin and unusual for this market, so the all in number is close to $21. The building dates to 1974, and that is the thing to weigh against the price.

What this search tells you

Your constraint is a monthly number, not a rate per foot

Your lender caps a monthly payment, so we rank by gross monthly cost rather than by asking rate. A 2,500 SF suite at $19 and a 5,000 SF suite at $17 are not close on your budget even though the rates look similar: they are $3,958 and $7,083 a month.

Operating expenses decide four of these, not the asking rate

Bluewater Bay 4536 and 1507 both ask $22.00 a foot. With operating expenses added they are $28.75 and $31.03 all in, so the office suite is the more expensive of the two despite the identical headline. Any card here showing operating expenses as Unlisted carries an unpriced gap we close with the landlord before comparing.

Niceville and Freeport buy you more room for the money

The lowest base rents in the search sit inland. Palm Plaza asks $17 to $19 a foot against $28.50 on Highway 98 in Santa Rosa Beach. The trade is drive time and patient draw, which is a question about how you bring patients in rather than a question about real estate.

Ground floor is the filter that removes most of this market

A dental build needs operatory plumbing, vacuum and compressor lines, equipment delivery, and post-sedation patient egress. That rules out upstairs suites almost automatically, and it is why several otherwise well-priced spaces on the corridor are not on this list.

Only one space here was built for the use

Bluewater Bay 4536 is listed as medical space in a grocery-anchored center with 33,000 vehicles a day. Everywhere else you are converting retail, office, or flex, and the fit-out benchmark for medical or office work runs roughly $180 a foot before dental equipment.

Lease term is an outcome of the build-out, not a starting point

A dental fit-out is the largest number in this deal, and much of it is money a landlord can put in as a tenant improvement allowance. The landlord recovers that allowance through rent across the term, so the length of the lease follows from how much they contribute. That is why no suggested term sits on these cards. We ask each landlord what they will fund first, then negotiate the term that amortizes it at a monthly payment your lender will accept. Expect that to be longer than a standard first lease, and treat the extra years as what the allowance costs rather than as a concession.

To confirm on your side

Your operatory count

Your target of 2,400 to 3,400 SF implies six to eight operatories at the 400 SF per operatory rule. Whether you are opening with six or building for eight changes which of these spaces work and what electrical service we ask for.

Your monthly ceiling

We have deliberately not chased the number from your lender, because an expensive building is a negotiation rather than a disqualification. Knowing the ceiling lets us decide where to push hardest.

Whether sedation is in the plan

If it is, the building likely needs to be sprinklered and a medical gas room may need direct outside ventilation. That is worth knowing before we shortlist.

Your open-by date

Two of these deliver on a schedule rather than immediately. Baytowne Office is available 1 February 2027 and 4935 is still under construction, so your target opening decides whether they stay on the list.

Whether the tour starts from Crestview

The drive order in this packet assumes it does. If you are coming from somewhere else the sequence changes, and so does the day.
